correctness.rationale: Each stationary scalar LQR plant term is J=(q+kᵀRk)g(a+bᵀk), g=(1−y²)⁻¹. Directional Hessian D²J=2z g+4u g′h+Q g″h², where u²≤zQ. Completing square yields D²J≥z(2g−4g′²/g″)=2z/(1+3y²)≥z/2. Summing gives Hess F≥Rbar/2 throughout convex joint stability slabs. Coercivity and blowup at finite stability boundaries ensure a unique interior minimum and PL inequality; explicit q_y=(1−y)^4, a_y=y(3+y²)/(1+3y²), k_y=y−a_y give Hess→1/2 from above, so sharp. Independent symbolic simplification and 400 random directional checks corroborate formulas; proof handles all dimensions of k but only scalar state.

A heterogeneity-independent explicit Hessian modulus for an arbitrary finite mixture of scalar-state plants with multi-input shared feedback, plus exact sharpness and unique optimality, is a reusable rigorous benchmark for policy optimization rather than a textbook restatement of individual scalar feedback formulas.
